Radyshevsky, a prominent conservative church figure and critic of Feofan Prokopovich, was appointed archimandrite of the Pskov-Caves Monastery in 1730 following the accession of Empress Anna Ioannovna. His tenure was cut short in 1731 when he was arrested, interrogated, and removed from office as Feofan reasserted control over his clerical opponents. This historical background directly accounts for the brief 1730–1731 tenure.

Therefore, the correct answer is **F. Markell**.

I support **G. Veniamin**.

To clarify why this is the correct choice over the other suggestions:

1. **Veniamin (Sakhnovsky)** served as archimandrite of the nearby Svyatogorsky Monastery from 1726 until 1730. In 1730, he was transferred to head the Pskov-Caves (Pskovo-Pechersky) Monastery. He held this position until July 1731, when he was consecrated to the episcopacy as Bishop of Kolomna and Kashira (and later transferred to Vyatka). This precise 1730–1731 window directly explains the brevity of his tenure.
2. The references to **Markell** (specifically Markell Radyshevsky / Rodyshevsky) appear to be a confusion with other monasteries; Markell's well-known conflicts with Feofan Prokopovich in 1730–1731 were tied to his roles elsewhere (notably as archimandrite of the Bizyukov Monastery), not the Pskov-Caves Monastery.

Therefore, the historical record firmly identifies the archimandrite from 1730 to 1731 as **G. Veniamin**.
